content.comment_body: Hello, As previously mentioned in another post, I'm new to [product_name] and its associated programming tool, currently exploring [version_no]. There are two main modes: diagram mode and network project mode. In diagram mode, I can create and save multiple diagrams separately. In network project mode, files are saved with a different extension, and I can add devices to diagrams as well. Most instructional videos I've seen use diagram mode, but some official training documents from [company_name] advise creating projects and not working directly in diagram mode. This has left me quite confused, as I couldn't find a clear explanation about the two modes and when each should be used. What’s the best approach: diagram mode or network project mode? Or under what circumstances should each be used? Thanks in advance.

It's really a matter of personal preference and each user should choose what fits their needs. Diagram mode is generally intended for programs that run on just one [product_name] and don't require interaction with other devices. Network project mode is best suited when your [product_name] needs to communicate with multiple devices, like other controllers, operator panels, or compatible systems.

For standalone programming, use the diagram mode (.lsc file format). The network project mode (.mnp) doesn’t provide extra value for single-device setups. Even with diagram mode, you can still connect to other devices (another controller, interface device, Modbus, or compatible systems) via the network connections menu. The software remembers and automatically opens the most recent diagram files, while network project files need to be opened manually. An advantage of network project mode is that you can search for compatible devices on the network—for example, if you are unsure of the device IP address. Otherwise, network mode can take up more screen space without additional benefits for simple setups.

In my experience, network mode makes it much easier to connect multiple devices together. Setting up connections between several controllers is straightforward in network mode compared to diagram mode, where it can be more involved.

analysis.insight_summary: Users commonly find it unclear which situations call for using diagram mode versus network project mode within [product_name] programming software. The available documentation and online materials do not sufficiently explain the workflow and benefits of each mode, which leads to confusion for newcomers. More seasoned users clarify that the choice should be based on the project requirements rather than strict technical limitations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want straightforward guidance on when to use diagram mode or network project mode in [product_name] programming tool. Specifically, they are looking for practical advice and best practices for creating individual device diagrams or handling multi-device network projects.
